_: Vendored-file manifest for oc-vendor-drift (issue #700). Each entry names a file this repo carries a copy of, the upstream revision it was flattened from, and the ONLY differences permitted. A delta entry matches OUR form via `match` and THEIR form via `match_upstream` (defaulting to `match`), because a delta line must be droppable from both sides or the comparison shifts. Anything else is drift and fails the guard.

vendor.why: Vendored copy of the Open Questions register. The delta below is the DEPLOYMENT difference only, re-flattened against f02eebe5 (#613) and every entry named by what it contains. Three block declarations were RETIRED here, not added: the #497 vocabulary-widening deltas and the 36-line `8e. #497` selftest block they guarded are gone because upstream now carries `resolved_mechanically` in CLOSED_STATUSES itself, so the divergence they described no longer exists -- a declaration of a divergence upstream has since absorbed is drift of the DECLARATION, and leaving it would have made the guard report a defect that was already fixed. The remaining blocks are comment rewraps declared in PAIRS (one `local`, one `upstream` half each) plus the deployment-only 8b3 battery. A block is an EXACT contiguous run stripped from its OWN side only; zero or two occurrences is DRIFTED, never a silent pass (#343), and each new block was widened with context until it occurred exactly once.

block: # The renderer's DEPENDENCY MANIFEST, shipped BESIDE it (#520, ruling n=3863,
# adopted here under #50). Node resolves a bare ESM import by walking up from the
# importing module's own directory, so the five packages oc-questions-render.mjs
# imports must be installed in render_dir() -- the directory the renderer is
# copied into and run from. Until this file existed the kit declared `node` on
# PATH and nothing else, so nothing tracked told a reader WHICH packages to
# install: the provisioning lived in an evidence directory no member reads, and
# on this box it was a hand-made untracked file in the build dir. The manifest is
# copied into the build dir as `package.json` by render_via_node() so the one
# step is `npm install` in that directory; the install itself stays MANUAL
# because it is a network operation and no gate may depend on network access.
delta.why: Dependency-manifest doctrine, deployment wording: names the adoption under this factory's #50 and keeps the local PROG-derived renderer name. The subject is the same declaration; the sentence says WHO adopted it.

block: # -- 8b3. THE RENDERER'S DEPENDENCY MANIFEST (#520 / factory #50). A page
# that cannot be provisioned by anyone reading the repo is a page whose
# next render is a coin flip: the packages lived in an evidence dir no
# reader consults, and on this box in a hand-made untracked build-dir
# file. NUMBERED 8b3, NOT 8d: 8d already belongs to C6 below, and two
# sections sharing a number make every "see 8d" reference ambiguous --
# the same drift class as a citation nobody can resolve. 8b3 also sits
# beside 8b2, the renderer section this one extends.
# Four legs, each naming the mutant it kills:
#   (i)   a fresh build dir receives BOTH render.mjs and package.json
#         -- mutant: the single-source copy, which leaves no manifest
#   (ii)  the placed manifest is byte-identical to the TRACKED one
#         -- mutant: writing a stale or hand-rolled manifest
#   (iii) every bare ESM specifier the renderer imports is DECLARED in
#         the manifest -- mutant: a manifest that omits react-dom, the
#         exact #520 defect (node resolves nothing, and the fault
#         arrives as ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND with no remedy on disk)
#   (iv)  an ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND reason NAMES the build dir and the
#         `npm install` step -- mutant: the bare rc string, which tells
#         a reader the render failed and nothing about the fix
_fresh = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="oq-manifest-")
_saved_render = os.environ.get("OC_QUESTIONS_RENDER_DIR")
try:
os.environ["OC_QUESTIONS_RENDER_DIR"] = _fresh
_m_html, _m_why = render_via_node({"root": "page", "elements": {}})
ck(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(_fresh, "render.mjs")),
"(i) a render places render.mjs in a FRESH build dir (%r)"
% (sorted(os.listdir(_fresh)),))
ck(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(_fresh, "package.json")),
"(i) ...and package.json BESIDE it, so `npm install` has a "
"manifest in the directory node resolves from; a single-source "
"copy leaves none and the page cannot be provisioned (%r)"
% (sorted(os.listdir(_fresh)),))
ck(os.path.isfile(RENDER_MANIFEST_SRC),
"(ii) the manifest is TRACKED beside the tool (%s), not only "
"hand-placed in a build dir" % (os.path.basename(RENDER_MANIFEST_SRC),))
_placed = open(os.path.join(_fresh, "package.json"),
encoding="utf-8").read()
_tracked = open(RENDER_MANIFEST_SRC, encoding="utf-8").read()
ck(_placed == _tracked,
"(ii) ...and the placed copy is byte-identical to the tracked one")
# (iii) STATIC sufficiency: no node, no network, no install -- the
# manifest must simply name every package the renderer imports.
_rsrc = open(RENDER_SRC, encoding="utf-8").read()
_bare = set()
for _m in re.finditer(r"""(?:from|import)\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]""", _rsrc):
_spec = _m.group(1)
if _spec.startswith(".") or _spec.startswith("/"):
continue
_bare.add("/".join(_spec.split("/")[:2])
if _spec.startswith("@")
else _spec.split("/")[0])
_declared = set(json.loads(_tracked).get("dependencies", {}))
ck(bool(_bare),
"(iii) the renderer's bare imports were actually EXTRACTED "
"(%r) -- an empty set would make the coverage leg vacuous"
% (sorted(_bare),))
ck(not (_bare - _declared),
"(iii) every bare ESM specifier the renderer imports is DECLARED "
"in the manifest (missing: %r)"
% (sorted(_bare - _declared),))
# (iv) The remedy is composed from the RUN's own stderr, so the leg
# drives a synthetic ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND rather than depending on
# whether this box happens to have node_modules installed.
_Proc = type("_Proc", (object,), {
"returncode": 1, "stdout": "",
"stderr": "Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package "
"'react-dom' imported from render.mjs"})
_real_run = subprocess.run
try:
subprocess.run = lambda *a, **kw: _Proc()
_r_html, _r_why = render_via_node({"root": "page", "elements": {}})
finally:
subprocess.run = _real_run
ck(_r_why and "npm install" in _r_why and _fresh in _r_why,
"(iv) an ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND reason names `npm install` AND the "
"build dir it must run in -- a declaration a reader cannot "
"discover is half a remedy (%r)" % (_r_why,))
# The remedy must be FAULT-SPECIFIC, not appended to every failure:
# a non-module fault keeps its own reason. Driven from a synthetic
# non-module stderr so the leg does not depend on this box having
# node_modules installed.
_Proc2 = type("_Proc2", (object,), {
"returncode": 1, "stdout": "",
"stderr": "Error: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useMemo')"})
try:
subprocess.run = lambda *a, **kw: _Proc2()
_n_html, _n_why = render_via_node({"root": "page", "elements": {}})
finally:
subprocess.run = _real_run
ck(_n_why and "npm install" not in _n_why,
"(iv) ...and the remedy is NOT bolted onto an unrelated fault: "
"a non-module fault keeps its own reason (%r)" % (_n_why,))
finally:
if _saved_render is None:
os.environ.pop("OC_QUESTIONS_RENDER_DIR", None)
else:
os.environ["OC_QUESTIONS_RENDER_DIR"] = _saved_render
shutil.rmtree(_fresh, ignore_errors=True)
delta.why: THE LOCAL 8b3 BATTERY (#520 / factory #50): four selftest legs proving the dependency manifest is placed beside the renderer, that a failed placement is a named fault, and that the declared packages match the renderer's imports. Deployment-only -- it exercises the local PROG-derived placement, so it has no upstream counterpart.

delta.match: ^    #   \* entry\["subject"\] is CREATION-ONLY \(:1516\): an immutable, set-level$

delta.why: #627's rationale cites the line where the home REFUSES a second --subject. That line number is per-home by construction: the two trees carry different declaration layers above it, so the deployment's guard sits at :1516 where upstream's sits at :1505. Copying upstream's number into this home would be a false citation pointing at the wrong line of its own file, so the difference is DECLARED here rather than erased. Measured 2026-11-07 against agent-factories dc957999c600, the tip that adopted #627 on both homes.

A shared number is impossible without renumbering a shipped section, and the label is a reader's map of the file, so each home carries its own. agent-factories' own questions-homes gate declares the same difference.
